name: Rand Paul

issue_poll.name: Pew Research Center national survey of registered voters, Oct 10–16, 2022
issue_poll.note: National fallback: no 2022 Kentucky poll ranking issues was found (Jan 2022 Mason-Dixon poll asked only approval and vote choice). Ranked by share calling each issue very important; 'future of democracy' dropped as not vote-testable; immigration and foreign policy tied at 54%, immigration taken for consistency with other files.

issues.position: Vote against new spending not paid for; balance the budget
issues.note: Campaign filing release also cites his Penny Plan: https://randpaul.com/dr-paul-files-for-re-election/

issues.position: Opposes government overreach and Medicare for All; no specific plan
issues.note: Coverage framed this as general philosophy, not a stated health policy.

issues.position: Opposes the Green New Deal agenda; no specific measure

issues.note: Direction only; no specific bill or policy named.

issues.position: Oppose federal funding or encouragement of red-flag laws
issues.note: No Senate floor vote on red-flag laws this term.

issues.position: Leave abortion to states; oppose a national ban

votes.question: Cloture on the motion to proceed

issues.note: No national ban got a floor vote; vote against federal abortion-rights bill read as consistent with leaving it to states.
2022 entries are mostly multi-senator letters (e.g. Title 42) whose signers were not confirmed.

caveats: Issue ranking uses national Pew polling; no 2022 Kentucky issue-ranking poll was found.
Paul skipped the only scheduled 2022 debate and ran few issue ads, so 7 of 10 issues have no specific campaign position.
Foreign policy (tied with immigration at 54%) was left out, though Paul campaigned on ending foreign wars and Ukraine-aid oversight.
H.R.3746 roll call 146 inferred from a vote-tracker URL; H.R.1968 roll call number not confirmed. Paul's vote on H.R.1968 from Deseret News (lone GOP no).
